A file reopened from the archive (November 2009, closed as a ‘training accident’):

· Álex Prieto (17) drowned at 23.00 at night when an eight capsized. Strap marks on his ankles; the file says ‘caught in the shoes’.
· Statement of the coach Javier Molina: ‘I was running the session.’ The statement was taken with the president Ramón Castillo present.
· One of the rowers in the boat: Gonzalo Castillo.
· Three weeks after the closure, a €600,000 ‘youth sports’ donation to the club from the Fundación Santa Ana.
The file closed as a ‘training accident’ twenty-one years ago has been reopened.

· Cause of death: drowning.
· Strap marks on both heels; abrasions on the ankles from trying to free his feet.
· No alcohol, no drugs. Heart sound.
· Time of death: 06.00–06.30.

· The drain plug in the stern is missing; the boat took in water at the stern and lost its balance within minutes.
· The emergency heel ties on the shoes were shortened with two black plastic cable ties: the feet can’t be pulled out. The cable ties were later cut; their cut ends are inside the boat.
· Overnight the boat was in the boathouse, on the victim’s rack.
The rower finds the capsized boat.
The president enters the boathouse and stays forty minutes.
The coach puts his boat on its rack; the plug is in place.
The coach arrives as he does every morning.
In the trophy cabinet, behind the 2009 cup
Where did the boat’s drain plug go?
It was recorded that the plug was found behind the 2009 cup.
The plug wasn’t in the river.
The plugs in the workshop were all accounted for.
The death was ruled an accident; on Monday Carmen Prieto came to bube alone.
Gonzalo Castillo was arrested; his father polished the trophies for the regatta.
Iker Salas was fired; the plug stayed in the cabinet.

Ramón Castillo was arrested; the 2009 file was reopened as ‘negligent homicide and destruction of evidence’, and Gonzalo Castillo will also stand trial. The Fundación Santa Ana donation was reported to the Triana branch.
Search of the president’s office and cabinet
The plug had been removed and the heel ties shortened with cable ties.
The son is one of those responsible for 2009, but that night he was at home and didn’t enter the boathouse; only his father is in the watchman’s log.
The maintenance man saw in the evening that the plug was in place, and he didn’t enter the boathouse at night.

The drain plug came out from behind the 2009 cup in his cabinet, with his print on it; the watchman saw him in the boathouse for forty minutes at night. The reopened 2009 file shows what the victim was going to tell, together with the mother.

Yes. I was nineteen. It was a game, a stupid game. We tied his feet, tipped the boat over; the rope was supposed to come loose. It didn’t. My father took care of everything. I didn’t kill Javier; since that night I can’t even go down to the boathouse. Last night I was at home; my wife woke up, ask her.
He straightens his polo collar and lowers his hand.
Were you in that boat in 2009?
I’m on the board; I don’t go down to the boathouse.
I’m at the gate, at night.

The boathouse opens with a card, and I write it in my log too. At 23.40 at night the president came; ‘I’ll check the trophies for tomorrow’s regatta,’ he said. He stayed forty minutes. Nobody else. Javier came at 05.45 in the morning, as always.
He smooths his moustache with his thumb.
Who entered the boathouse during the night?

Javier prepares it himself; he doesn’t let anyone touch it. Last night at six I saw him put it on his rack; the plug was in, I checked; the heel ties were normal. The cable ties are our workshop’s; the box is next to the boathouse door, anyone can take them.
He scrapes the varnish stain on his hands with a fingernail.
He drowned in a boat with its plug removed and its heel ties shortened
A rowing coach drowned under the Triana Bridge with his feet tied into his boat.

Ramón Castillo’s office at the club and the trophy cabinet (with the branch chief’s approval):

· Behind the 2009 championship cup in the cabinet, the drain plug of the victim’s boat; Ramón Castillo’s fingerprint on the plug.
· In his desk drawer, a bundle from the boathouse workshop’s box of cable ties; the cut ends match those in the boat.
· On his phone, 18 October, to an unregistered number: ‘Javier goes on Monday.’ Reply: ‘I told you, not a second time.’
PRESIDENT’S OFFICE AND TROPHY CABINET — SEARCH
38, the president’s son; a former rower at the club, now on the board.
61, mother of the young rower who drowned in 2009.

Álex was seventeen. A night training session, they said; the eight capsized, everyone got out, he didn’t. An accident. Last month Javier knocked on my door. ‘Carmen, there was no training session that night,’ he said. ‘The big lads used to throw the little ones in the water; it was a tradition. Gonzalo’s crew tied Álex’s feet. I saw it; the president said keep quiet.’ On Monday he was going to come to bube with me.
She takes the locket at her neck into her palm.
Mother of the rower who drowned in 2009.
I’ve been waiting twenty-one years for an answer.
This club is a hundred years old; presidents come and go, the club stays.
I protected my son. What father wouldn’t?

On Monday Javier was going to go to bube with that woman. Gonzalo would go to prison, and me, and the donation, and the foundation… In 2009 the adviser at the foundation told me, ‘We’ll sort this once, not a second time.’ I took out the plug, I shortened the ties with cable ties; whatever happened to Álex happened. I put the plug behind the cup. The 2009 cup.
I looked at the trophies, for the regatta. I didn’t even go near Javier’s boat. He was getting old; a wave, a cramp.
He does up the button of his blazer.
Were you in the boathouse last night?
2009 was an accident, and this club put it behind it long ago.

On the morning of 19 October 2030, on the Guadalquivir under the Triana Bridge, the rowing club’s coach Javier Molina (57) was found dead beneath his capsized single scull, his feet tied into the boat’s shoes.

The rower Valeria Cruz found the body at 06.50 as she went out to train. The night watchman Hamid Benali was at the club overnight. The club president Ramón Castillo, board member Gonzalo Castillo and maintenance man Iker Salas arrived in the morning.
Request permission to open the 2009 file from the archive
Request an examination of the boat
Request permission to search the president’s office and trophy cabinet

The mother, the son and the maintenance man told of 2009 and of yesterday’s boat; those got the archive opened. The watchman’s log showed only the president in the boathouse at night. The search found the plug behind the cup.
What happened to Álex happened to Javier; only this time nobody laughed.

In 2009, for the sake of a ‘tradition’, the crew of the president’s son Gonzalo Castillo tied seventeen-year-old Álex Prieto’s feet and capsized the boat; Álex drowned. The president Ramón Castillo had the coach give a false statement, the file closed, the foundation’s donation arrived. Twenty-one years later the coach Javier Molina decided to speak, together with the mother. At night in the boathouse Ramón removed his boat’s plug, shortened the heel ties with cable ties and hid the plug behind the 2009 cup.

His boat was upside down, caught on the bridge pier. I jumped in, tried to pull his feet out; they wouldn’t come. The heel ties were short; I’d never seen them like that. I cut them with my knife. I was too late.
She holds the towel on her shoulder with both hands.
The drain plug from the stern of the single scull; it came out from behind a trophy cabinet.
Two black cable ties fitted to the heel ties of the boat’s shoes and later cut.
The 2009 championship cup in the club’s cabinet; the names of eight rowers beneath it.
